answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybils the way a lagoon resists a flood: every new agent must lock collateral behind a juniper-strong identity bond that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues slowly, like shale laid down layer by layer, and only aged, bonded agents earn attestation weight, so cheap sockpuppets stay weightless while the attacker's bill grows with every identity minted.
